claim: On average, neural network model latency on MCUs varies approximately linearly with the model's operation (op) count under a uniform prior over models in the search space, allowing op count to serve as a cheap proxy for latency/energy during neural architecture search.
stance_target: feasibility of efficient neural architecture search for MCU-targeted TinyML models without expensive hardware-in-the-loop latency measurement
scope_conditions: MCU-class hardware, differentiable NAS search spaces
quoted_support: we observe an intriguing property of NAS search spaces for MCU model design: on average, model latency varies linearly with model operation (op) count under a uniform prior over models in the search space.

claim: MicroNet models achieve state-of-the-art results on all three MLPerf Tiny industry-standard benchmark tasks: visual wake words, audio keyword spotting, and anomaly detection.
stance_target: viability of NAS-derived compact architectures for audio/vision TinyML tasks relevant to ECE embedded projects
quoted_support: MicroNets demonstrate state-of-the-art results for all three TinyMLperf industry-standard benchmark tasks: visual wake words, audio keyword spotting, and anomaly detection.
